title: A Wealth Tax Would Harm California
gist: Laura Tyson and Lenny Mendonca argue California's Proposition 40, a one-time 5% wealth tax on roughly 250 billionaires resident on January 1, 2026, is poorly designed. Because wealth is mobile, targeted billionaires are likely to leave the state, taking future income-tax revenue with them.

insights.claim: California's Proposition 40 (Billionaire Tax Act) would impose a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of an estimated 250 individuals worth over $1 billion who resided in California on January 1, 2026, and needs only a simple majority of voters to pass.
insights.speaker: @LauraDTyson
insights.so_what: Defines the scope of a ballot measure directly affecting founder/insider holdings of California-based tech wealth.
insights.quote: would impose a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of an estimated 250 individuals with a net worth exceeding $1 billion who resided in California on January 1, 2026
insights.locator: BERKELEY—Six Nobel laureate economists recently signed

insights.claim: Six Nobel laureate economists have signed an open letter supporting California's Proposition 40 billionaire wealth tax.
insights.speaker: @LauraDTyson
insights.so_what: Shows elite economist backing, raising the measure's perceived legitimacy and odds of passage.

insights.claim: Laura Tyson and Lenny Mendonca judge California's proposed one-time billionaire wealth tax to be poorly designed and likely to do more harm than good.
insights.speaker: @LauraDTyson
insights.so_what: Prominent economists opposing the measure signals a contested fiscal-policy fight in a key US tech state.
insights.quote: We believe the proposal is poorly designed and likely to do more harm than good.
insights.locator: BERKELEY—Six Nobel laureate economists recently signed

insights.claim: Because wealth is mobile, billionaires facing a California wealth tax are likely to leave the state, taking their future income-tax payments with them and eroding long-run revenue.
insights.speaker: @LauraDTyson
insights.so_what: Billionaire out-migration could shrink California's income-tax base and pressure state finances and municipal credit.
insights.quote: Since wealth is mobile, those who stand to lose the most will simply leave, taking their future income-tax payments with them.

insights.claim: A one-time wealth levy's upfront revenue gain for California could be outweighed by the loss of future income-tax revenue from departing billionaires.
insights.speaker: @LauraDTyson
insights.so_what: Voters and bond investors should weigh net, not gross, fiscal effects of the levy.
